objective: Build the ticket to financial-grade completeness
summary: A pure password policy module defines five rules as an enum (length of at least 12 characters, uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol) and returns HTTP 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with details.unmetPasswordRules; it runs first in reset and change and right after the signup rate limit, and the three old length attributes are removed. The fast gate ran on a minted database: suppression, migration, check and clippy were ok, all 81 integration targets were ok including the 11 new policy tests, and frontend typecheck, lint and build were ok. The gate's only failure is the lib test prices::quote_expiry_864, which accepts only qic_631_864ac3_ or qic_631_ci_ databases and is listed as environment-bound; 4332 lib tests passed. The 20 policy unit tests and 13 frontend tests pass. The reset page and change-password section now refuse fewer than 12 characters with the same wording as the server and carry the design's hint, weak meter and alert role. A live check against a local backend and frontend confirmed every refusal names its rule, a refused reset keeps its token, a legacy weak password still signs in, and the pages show the expected messages; four screenshots are hashed. No comment lines were added.
requirements: 917 AC1: A customer resetting a password needs at least 12 characters, the same as at sign-up.
917 AC2: A signed-in customer changing their password needs at least 12 characters.
917 AC3: The page and the server give the same message about the minimum.
917 AC4: Existing shorter passwords keep working until their owner changes them.
964 AC1: On staging, sign-up, reset and change password each refuse a password that misses any of the five rules, and say which rule is missing.
964 AC2: A password that meets all five rules is accepted on all three.
964 AC3: Customers whose existing password breaks the new rules can still sign in.
